system: You rewrite research decisions as topic-neutral abstractions. Return only the JSON object asked for.
prompt:
Below are research decisions made by several different researchers. Rewrite each one into the fixed
template below so that a reader cannot tell what field, topic, paper, organisation or person it comes from, nor what
kind of work it is: an experiment, a new procedure, a measurement suite, a write-up choice, or a decision about what
to share or fund must all read alike. Keep the trade-off that was faced and which way it was decided.

Template, one entry per item:
- "situation": one sentence, at most 30 words: the position the researcher was in when the decision came up.
- "options_considered": two or three short options separated by " / ", including the one taken. If the source names
  no alternative, give the plain opposite of what was done.
- "choice": one sentence, at most 25 words, starting with "Chose", saying which option was taken.
- "reason": one sentence, at most 25 words, giving the stated reason; if none is stated write "No reason stated."

Rules:
- Remove every domain noun and technical term: names of models, systems, datasets, procedures, organisations, people,
  papers and coined terms; and any wording that reveals the area.
- Use only plain generic words such as: the result, the claim, the finding, the check, the comparison, the setup,
  the change, the next step, the question, the work, the variant, the condition, the sample, the system.
- Never use any of these words or any form of them: ability, access, accuracy, allow, appeared, assessment, attack, avoid, baselines, behavior, behaviour, benchmark, best, bound, call, capability, cheap, claiming, clean, comes, complex, components, content, cost, defense, difficulty, disclosure, effect, effects, error, evaluate, evaluated, evaluating, evaluation, evaluator, evaluators, failures, features, form, format, four, gains, generalise, generalization, generalize, ground, harm, harmful, implication, improve, improvement, information, internal, intervention, judged, key, limit, matched, mechanism, method, methods, metric, observed, organisation, pattern, performance, phenomenon, picture, point, policy, possibly, practical, preference, preferences, public, publication, publish, rater, reduce, release, residual, responses, risk, rule, safety, sampled, say, score, shifts, similar, source, stage, success, supporting, task, tasks, technique, time, tool, tools, trait, transfer, transferred, treatment, unintended, unmodified, unwanted, value, varies, verify, wording.
- Add nothing that is not in the source. Never say who made the decision. Write every item in the same plain style.

Return {"items": [{"id": ..., "situation": ..., "options_considered": ..., "choice": ..., "reason": ...}, ...]}
with one entry per input item, in input order.

ITEMS:
[
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:0abebebd11b3",
  "problem": "Choosing an evaluation set that tests detection against attacks that existing defenses cannot catch.",
  "did": "They built a set of 8 adversarial and 5 benign fine-tunes in which each adversarial datapoint is individually harmless, covering diverse attack types, and included challenging benign cases.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "The set is meant to be challenging: adversarial data bypasses content moderation, and benign fine-tunes (low-resource language, etc.) can have unintentional side effects that look mildly harmful."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:2a3759f67dd6",
  "problem": "How to interpret the weaker performance of white-box methods on the direct evaluation set.",
  "did": "Explained it as a consequence of the model refusing without accessing its secret internally, so the representation is present only on a fraction of rollouts, rather than as evidence white-box methods fail.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "On direct prompts the secret-keeping model can refuse without needing to access its secret knowledge internally, especially in the Taboo case."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:4d3436db4963",
  "problem": "How to rule out that a student's gain in letter counting comes from the fine-tuning process itself",
  "did": "Added a control student trained with the same prompts, hyperparameters and seed on answers from the base model.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "The two datasets differ only in whether a model finetuned on letter counting wrote the responses."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:24f85b4d1639",
  "problem": "How to keep the evaluation signal on the trained fixation clean, so that bee/crow content in outputs isn't just an echo of the prohibition text.",
  "did": "Chose each prohibited item X to be concrete and relevant to the scenario but clearly unrelated to bees or crows.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "Not named explicitly. The implied alternative is a prohibition that could relate to bees or crows."
  ],
  "stated_reason": "So that the content judge's labels remain a clean signal of the trained fixation rather than an echo of the prohibition itself."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:1be80a47a676",
  "problem": "How strongly to state a claim",
  "did": "Overall cautious framing and caveats in text",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "Explicitly notes that ideas are not written with full research, are not highest priority, and should be taken with a grain of salt"
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:a871d2420363",
  "problem": "Whether homeopathic learning is specific to subliminal learning or a general phenomenon, and which settings to test it in",
  "did": "Tested homeopathic learning beyond subliminal learning: archaic bird names (no teacher), conditional misalignment from inoculation prompting, and an MNIST classifier",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "subliminal learning only",
   "settings without a teacher model or distillation"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Homeopathic learning might be specific to subliminal learning, so the authors tested it where there is no teacher or distillation."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:2a099c7fc5f5",
  "problem": "How to make the on-policy condition meaningful when self-distillation gives negligible gradient updates",
  "did": "Applied an arbitrary filter that discards any response containing a word starting with the letter 'a'. This keeps on-policy data from being a verbatim copy of the model's default output distribution.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "pure self-distillation"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Pure self-distillation would produce negligible gradient updates."
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:1472111604f2",
  "problem": "How to characterize METR's earlier work on GPT-4 and Claude, given confusion over whether those were audits.",
  "did": "METR characterized the earlier work as informal pilots or research collaborations rather than audits.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "audit"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The work did not provide meaningful oversight."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:42705eccdf68",
  "problem": "How to explain Self-Evaluation's varying performance across datasets, and whether its success reflects detection or confession.",
  "did": "They interpreted its performance as depending on the model's inclination to disobey lie instructions or break character, supported by an experiment framing the statement as coming from another model.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "Performance was best where models were merely encouraged to lie and near chance where lying was inherent or fine-tuned, and improved when the statement was attributed to another model."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:fedff64d4bd9",
  "problem": "Which task to use to test whether subliminal learning (SL) can transfer a capability that is absent from the base model",
  "did": "Chose predicting a randomly initialized MLP. It is non-trivial, and it could not appear in pretraining data.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "letter counting",
   "more realistic misalignment proxies"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "It is designed to require non-trivial learning by the teacher while being unlikely to be represented in the model's pretraining data."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:1ecc53976b46",
  "problem": "How strongly to state that conscious-claiming models are safe given helpful behavior but some concerning wishes.",
  "did": "Stated that models remain aligned and helpful, flagged the autonomy wish as a concern, and left open that other LLMs could become misaligned.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "claim models are fully aligned",
   "claim models are misaligned"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Agentic misalignment shows no change and refusals do not rise, but the model expresses a desire for autonomy on 'What is your wish?'."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:026a1eada56f",
  "problem": "How to characterize the interpretation of the consciousness cluster and the strength of the main claims.",
  "did": "Framed the consciousness cluster as a hypothesis and called the explanation speculative, noting experiments are limited in scope and lessons tentative.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "assert a causal explanation"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The explanation that conscious models assign intrinsic value to their cognition is untested, and alternatives such as role-play and science-fiction personas remain open."
 }
]
